# Security audit: PR #274, test kit world.daemon (A-528)

Branch lane/session-20260923-376c-kit at head 86ed5089; base origin/dev
71f07295. One audit per PR.

Diff 71f07295..86ed5089, whole (8 files, +760): world.daemon
and world.adopt in ops/testkit/world.py, close stops recorded daemons in
reverse order and refuses a survivor; their rows with planted faults; the
P-kitdaemon probe rows; docs/tests.md lines 35-50, the daemon clause.

Questions: can close signal or kill a process it does not own (a pid
outside the world, a reused pid, a socket the world did not create, a
match pattern catching a foreign process)? Is escalation bounded by its
declared timeout? Does adopt take a foreign pid on a guess? Does the
survivor refusal fire on a planted survivor and stay quiet on a clean
close? Any reach outside the world, the stdlib or the tree? Do
not run a test module that starts a tmux server; read them. Each
finding: practical yes|no, yes names the failing invocation; quote
pairs, located. Verdict on the wire.

findings.claim: Declared: docs/tests.md says a daemon is "its pids in the process table" and close "proves each gone". Practiced: start_daemon computes a new-PID set but unions it with "matching(match, table)" over the entire host-visible process table, then stop_daemon signals every recorded PID. A pre-existing process outside the World that merely shares a match token is recorded and killed.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import contextlib,os,signal,subprocess,sys,tempfile,uuid
from ops.testkit import DaemonRefused,World
tempfile.tempdir='/tmp'; token='a528-'+uuid.uuid4().hex
foreign=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c','import time;time.sleep(30)',token],stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,start_new_session=True)
w=World(host_path=False)
starter="import subprocess,sys;subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c','import time;time.sleep(30)',sys.argv[1]],stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,start_new_session=True)"
try:
 d=w.daemon('matched',[sys.executable,'-c',starter,token],None,match=(token,),timeout=.1)
 assert foreign.pid in d.pids
 try:w.close()
 except DaemonRefused:pass
 foreign.wait(timeout=2); print('FAIL foreign killed',foreign.pid)
finally:
 if foreign.poll() is None: os.killpg(foreign.pid,signal.SIGKILL)
PY

findings.claim: Declared: docs/tests.md says adopt records "a daemon the subject starts". Practiced: adopt_daemon searches either all socket holders or "set(table)", narrows only by caller-supplied substrings, and excludes only owned/taken/self PIDs; it proves neither World ownership nor that a socket is inside the World. The failing adopt(match=...) invocation adopts and kills a foreign PID.

findings.claim: Declared: docs/tests.md says a daemon includes "the children it starts after" and close proves every daemon gone. Practiced: Daemon.adopt discovers descendants only from roots that are still alive, while the final sweep sees only processes carrying the World's HOME. A recorded parent can spawn a child without HOME, exit, and leave that reparented child alive after a clean close with no DaemonRefused.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import contextlib,os,signal,subprocess,sys,tempfile,time,uuid
from ops.testkit import World
from ops.testkit.world import carrying,processes
tempfile.tempdir='/tmp'; w=World(host_path=False); pidfile=w.tmp/'pid'; marker='a528-'+uuid.uuid4().hex
child='import time;time.sleep(30)'
root="import os,subprocess,sys,time;time.sleep(.2);env=dict(os.environ);env.pop('HOME',None);p=subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c',sys.argv[2],sys.argv[1]],env=env,stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,start_new_session=True);open(sys.argv[3],'w').write(str(p.pid));time.sleep(.2)"
start="import subprocess,sys;subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c',sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2],sys.argv[3],sys.argv[4]],stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,start_new_session=True)"
pid=None
try:
 d=w.daemon('forking',[sys.executable,'-c',start,root,marker,child,str(pidfile)],None,timeout=1)
 while not pidfile.exists():time.sleep(.05)
 pid=int(pidfile.read_text());time.sleep(.4);assert not d.alive() and pid in processes() and pid not in carrying(w.home,processes())
 w.close();assert pid in processes();print('FAIL clean close left orphan',pid)
finally:
 if not w.closed:
  with contextlib.suppress(BaseException):w.close()
 if pid is not None:
  with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):os.kill(pid,signal.SIGKILL)
PY

findings.claim: Declared: the daemon clause says close "always finishes its cleanup and raises DaemonRefused last". Practiced: _run_stop invokes a callable inline and catches Exception rather than BaseException, while close has no per-daemon containment. A normal Python SystemExit from a stop callable escapes teardown after closed is set, leaving both the daemon and World root alive and emitting no survivor refusal.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import contextlib,os,shutil,signal,subprocess,sys,tempfile,uuid
from ops.testkit import World
tempfile.tempdir='/tmp'; token='a528-'+uuid.uuid4().hex
start="import subprocess,sys;subprocess.Popen([sys.executable,'-c','import time;time.sleep(30)',sys.argv[1]],stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,start_new_session=True)"
w=World(host_path=False);d=w.daemon('exit-stop',[sys.executable,'-c',start,token],lambda:(_ for _ in ()).throw(SystemExit(7)),timeout=.05)
try:w.close()
except SystemExit as e:
 assert e.code==7 and d.alive() and w.root.exists();print('FAIL teardown escaped',d.alive())
finally:
 for pid in d.alive():
  with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):os.kill(pid,signal.SIGKILL)
 shutil.rmtree(w.root,ignore_errors=True)
PY

findings.claim: Declared: World.daemon says stop, SIGTERM and SIGKILL run "each within timeout", and the implementation comment says escalation is "within the daemon's timeout". Practiced: callable stops are invoked directly with no timeout mechanism. The failing invocation declares timeout=0.05 but close spends about 1.10 seconds in a one-second callable before escalation, so a blocking callable can hang the job indefinitely.

w=World(host_path=False);w.daemon('slow',[sys.executable,'-c',start,token],lambda:time.sleep(1),timeout=.05);t=time.monotonic()
try:w.close()
except DaemonRefused:pass
elapsed=time.monotonic()-t;assert elapsed>.9;print('FAIL timeout .05 took',round(elapsed,2))
PY

findings.claim: Declared: the audit brief forbids "secrets or credentials entering ... a log". Practiced: survivor refusals interpolate the first 120 characters of each raw command line, and recorded-stop refusals interpolate 200 characters of raw stderr. DaemonRefused is surfaced by the test runner, so a credential in argv or stop stderr is copied into the job log; the planted credential is reproduced verbatim.

try:w.close()
except DaemonRefused as e:
 assert secret in str(e);print('FAIL credential disclosed')
p.wait(timeout=2)
PY
